But is that maybe downstream? R2 target is timing relation. Need preserve uncertainty. Could mention "the relevant assumption that King Michael is the author is supported by C1/C2" maybe used_claims. But residual should not ask if author? C1 states letter from King Michael to President. So author established. Need accession. Return JSON.

So establish date of King Michael's coming to power (relevant reign/accession). That's one.

Potential issue: If Michael first came to power 1927? But he was king 1927-1930, again 1940-1947. The letter in 1945 author King Michael. "come to power" might refer to 1944 coup? He wasn't newly come to power in 1944? Actually Michael became king in 1940, but was a figurehead under Antonescu; on Aug 23 1944 he led coup and took power. Letter March 1945 about six months after coup. So the requirement may refer to author came to power roughly six months before March 1945, i.e., Aug 1944. But without outside knowledge. Need research objective: establish when King Michael of Romania came to power (or assumed effective power) relative to March 1945. But "come to power" could be ambiguous. We should preserve "author had come to power" with author identified as King Michael.
